entities.name: Masjid Al-Ansar
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Masjid Al-Ansar (Arabic: مسجد الأنصار, Mosque of the Helpers/Supporters) in Singapore's Bedok area is one of Singapore's significant mosques, named for the Ansar — the Medinese Muslims who welcomed and supported the Prophet Muhammad and the Meccan Muslim migrants (Muhajirin) when they arrived in Medina during the Hijra of 622 CE. The Ansar's welcoming of the Muhajirin is one of the most celebrated acts of solidarity in Islamic history, representing the ideal of Islamic brotherhood.

The name 'Al-Ansar' (the Helpers/Supporters) carries deep Islamic historical resonance: the Ansar were the Medinese tribes (primarily the Aws and Khazraj, who converted to Islam) who offered refuge to the persecuted Meccan Muslims and shared their resources with the new arrivals. The Prophet Muhammad is recorded as saying that the Ansar occupy a special place in his heart, and they are frequently honored in Islamic tradition as exemplars of generosity and solidarity.

Singapore's Masjid Al-Ansar serves the Bedok area's Malay-Muslim community alongside Masjid Al-Amin, reflecting the density of Singapore's eastern residential areas and the mosque needs of the Muslim population. The mosque's name — evoking the ideal of welcoming and supporting newcomers — may hold particular significance in Singapore's multicultural context, where the Malay-Muslim community as a minority has had to navigate between hosting roles and minority status.
